## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical Kubernetes debugging skills, focusing on actionable steps, not theory. It checks familiarity with pod lifecycle, init containers, and how to correlate events with configuration objects during startup delays.

## Key Concepts

- Pod lifecycle and init containers
- kubectl debugging commands (describe, get, logs, jsonpath)
- Image pull behavior and identifiers
- ConfigMaps and Secrets mounting in pods
- Deployment rollout and readiness checks

```javascript
// Example diagnostic sequence (pseudo-commands, replace <pod> and <ns> accordingly)
kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>

kubectl describe deployment <deploy> -n <ns>

kubectl get secret -n <ns>
```

- How would you distinguish between a misconfigured readinessProbe vs a slow startup?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests end-to-end security design for multi-cloud Kubernetes workloads, focusing on identity, secret management, and policy enforcement with real-world tools.

## Key Concepts
- Zero-trust workload identity (SPIRE)
- Ephemeral credentials (Vault)
- Service mesh security (Istio, mTLS, AuthorizationPolicies)
- Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego)
- Egress controls to data lake and namespace isolation

## Sample Solution

### 1. SPIRE Workload Identity
```yaml
# spire-workload.yaml
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: data-platform-workload
spec:
  names:
    - data-service
    - analytics-service
    - etl-service
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: production
```

### 2. Vault Integration for Secrets
```yaml
# vault-secret-store.yaml
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultSecret
metadata:
  name: data-lake-credentials
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  vaultAddress: https://vault.data-platform.svc.cluster.local:8200
  path: secret/data-lake
  provider: hcp
  refreshInterval: 1h
```

### 3. Istio AuthorizationPolicy
```yaml
# istio-authz.yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: data-lake-access
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: data-lake-gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://data-platform/data-service"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
        paths: ["/v1/tables/*"]
```

### 4. OPA Policy Example
```rego
#.rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.namespace == "restricted"
  not input.request.object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  msg = "Pods must run as non-root"
}

allow[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  input.request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged
  msg = "Privileged containers not allowed"
}
```

### 5. CI Enforcement Check
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  opa-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run OPA policy check
        run: |
          opa eval --fail-defined-deny \
            --data policy.rego \
            --input manifests/
```

## Key Takeaways
- SPIRE provides cryptographically secure workload identity
- Vault enables dynamic secret rotation without application changes
- Istio mTLS ensures service-to-service encryption
- OPA/Rego enforces admission control and runtime policies

## Why This Is Asked

Tests end-to-end image provenance across multi-cloud GPU workloads, combining CI, runtime policies, and verification in real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance, Cosign, Sigstore, reproducible builds
- Kubernetes admission control (Kyverno/OPA)
- Buildx/OCI digests and registry security
- GPU workload constraints and cross-cloud policy

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: build, sign, verify
name: BuildSignVerify
on: [push]
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up QEMU/Buildx
      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          docker buildx create --use
          image=registry.example.com/project/image:${{ github.sha }}
          docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
            -t $image --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1 .
          cosign sign -key cosign.key $image
          docker push $image
      - name: Verify signature
        run: cosign verify -key cosign.pub $image
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-image
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: check-cosign-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    verifyImages:
    - image: registry.example.com/*
      pattern: "^.+$"
```

```yaml

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: guest-deploy
spec:

    spec:
      containers:

```

```yaml

kind: Deployment
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to translate security requirements into a enforceable policy and CI flow for a multi-tenant cluster. It also evaluates practical policy testing across PRs.

## Key Concepts

- Kyverno ClusterPolicy for container securityContext checks
- Kubernetes pod/spec validation in Deployments/StatefulSets
- CI gate integration with PR workflows
- Test manifests to verify both compliant and non-compliant cases

## Code Example

```javascript
// Kyverno policy (as YAML in practice)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-privileged-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-secctx
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job"]
    validate:
      message: "Container must drop ALL capabilities, run as non-root, and readOnly rootfs"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop:
                    - ALL
```

- How to test locally with sample manifests?

## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of Kubernetes manifests is a practical, repeatable gate in real projects. This tests understanding of policy-as-code, tooling choices (Kyverno vs Gatekeeper), constraint design for host access controls and image source controls, and CI integration in GitHub Actions with ephemeral test clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper
- Constraints for host access (hostNetwork, hostPath, hostPort, privileged containers)
- Image source controls (allowed registries) and imagePullPolicy enforcement
- CI integration in GitHub Actions using KinD or similar ephemeral clusters

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-host-access
spec:
  rules:
  - name: block-host-network
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
  - name: block-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not allowed"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ contains(element.volumes[].hostPath, '') }}"
          operator: "NotEqual"
          value: ""
```

## Minimal Policy (Combined)
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: security-guardrails
spec:
  rules:
  - name: deny-host-network-port
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork and hostPort are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
          hostPort: "0"
  - name: deny-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not permitted"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ @ }}"
          operator: "AnyNotIn"
          value: [""]
      foreach:
        - list: "spec.volumes[?hostPath]"
          deny: true
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              privileged: "false"
  - name: allowed-registries
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Images must come from approved registries"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "registry.company.com/*"
            imagePullPolicy: "Always"
```

## Failing Manifest (hostPath + hostNetwork)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: docker.io/myapp:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: host-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: host-volume
    hostPath:
      path: /etc
```

## Passing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.com/myapp:v1.0
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Validation
```bash
# Install Kyverno locally
brew install kyverno

# Apply policies
kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml

# Validate a manifest
kyverno validate insecure-pod.yaml
```

## CI Validation (GitHub Actions)
```yaml
name: Validate Manifests
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Create KinD cluster
      run: kind create cluster
    - name: Install Kyverno
      run: |
        kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
        kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=kyverno -n kyverno --timeout=120s
    - name: Apply policies
      run: kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f insecure-pod.yaml || echo "Expected failure"
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f secure-pod.yaml
```

## Code Example
```python
import csv, sys
from datetime import datetime

EXPECTED = {
  'id': int,
  'date': 'date',
  'amount': float,
  'category': str
}

DATE_FMT = '%Y-%m-%d'

def parse_row(row):
  row['id'] = int(row['id'])
  row['date'] = datetime.strptime(row['date'], DATE_FMT).date()
  row['amount'] = float(row['amount'])
  row['category'] = str(row['category'])
  return row

def main(path):
  with open(path, newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    header = set(reader.fieldnames or [])
    if header != set(EXPECTED.keys()):
      print('Header mismatch:', reader.fieldnames)
      sys.exit(1)
    for r in reader:
      try:
        parse_row(r)
      except Exception as e:
        print('Type/Parse error', e, r)
        sys.exit(1)
  print('OK')

if __name__ == '__main__':
  sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1]))
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests end-to-end security for ML artifacts, combining signing attestations, GitOps, and runtime policy in Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore Cosign sign-blob attest and verify-blob
- Model provenance and SBOM
- GitOps with Argo CD
- Admission policies: OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign a model blob and create an attestation
cosign sign-blob -key cosign.key models/model-v1.bin
cosign attest -key cosign.key --predicate predicate.json models/model-v1.bin
cosign verify-blob -key cosign.pub models/model-v1.bin
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy requiring attestation before deployment
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-model-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: attested-model-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: Attestation required for model artifact
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations.cosign_attested: "true"
```

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign_attested"] == "true"
  msg = "Model artifact must be attested with cosign before deployment"
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design policy-driven hardening for a multi-tenant Kubernetes platform, combining mutation and validation. It probes knowledge of securityContext, egress controls, and harnessing Gatekeeper or Kyverno in CI.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes Pod securityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop capabilities
- Policy types: mutation vs. validation
- Gatekeeper vs Kyverno: templates, constraints, and tests
- CI verification: unit tests, kubectl apply, and dry-run checks

## Code Example

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  container := input.request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_]
  not container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  msg = "container must set runAsNonRoot: true"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this locally with kind/k3d and Gatekeeper?
- How would you handle existing deployments that lack securityContext without downtime?
